title: Roman chord numbers
summary: Letters show both number and chord type.

steps.title: Roman chord numbers
steps.body:
**Roman numeral** means a number written with letters. For chords, I is 1, II is 2, III is 3, IV is 4, V is 5, VI is 6 and VII is 7. Uppercase marks major; lowercase marks minor; ° marks diminished. A major key has I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi, vii°.

**Why it matters:** The written number tells you the root’s scale degree and the chord type together.

steps.title: See it on the fretboard
steps.body: In G major, Em is vi: E is the sixth scale note and the triad is minor. C is IV, D is V and G is I.

items.prompt: Play E, G and B together. Use any positions for these notes.

steps.title: Explore the sounds
steps.body: Compare vi and VI on paper. The small letters are part of the instruction, not decoration.
